description: The one window, and only what a window needs. The shell reaches its own files over frank:// and Studio over fetch; the TEN commands it calls are sync_discover (job 26, 6 Sep) -- the Bonjour browse behind the Sync button -- google_sign_in (job 26b, 6 Sep) -- Google's consent page in the system browser, which Google will not show in a web view -- and audio_session_start (job 8b, 6 Sep) -- which takes the AVAudioSession when the reader first plays, so the audio survives the app switcher; those three through window.TTSTVHost, which lib.rs injects. It takes no argument and can only make this app's own sound keep playing, which is the whole of what a page could do with it. And (G-PULL, 11 Sep) the four book commands -- book_put, book_meta, book_list, book_remove -- through window.TTSTVHost.books: the Cache API refuses frank://, so a book a Sync pulls is written to <app data>/books/ and served back by the frank:// handler; every name they take is checked (a slug, a hash, a path inside the book's folder, refused in words otherwise) and they can reach nothing outside that folder. And (G-SYNCBG, 11 Sep) the three pull commands -- sync_start, sync_status, sync_stop -- through window.TTSTVHost.sync: a Sync's books are downloaded by the app on a thread of its own, so leaving the Settings page no longer cancels them; sync_start takes a job the page built (the books, their files, the Drive token or the LAN pairing), checks every name in it before a byte is fetched, fetches only from Drive's files endpoint or the paired Studio's paths, and writes only through the book door's own functions into <app data>/books/ -- or, for a job of kind language (G-LANG, 11 Sep), through the pack door into <app data>/languages/. And the three pack commands -- dict_langs, dict_lookup, dict_remove -- through window.TTSTVHost.dict: a word looked up in a language pack (one SQLite file per language, opened read-only), the packs on this phone listed, one removed; every name they take is a language code, checked, and they reach nothing outside <app data>/languages/. And (C2/K8, 13 Sep) one read-only command -- inbox_list -- which lists what a share put into this phone: the folders a share extension wrote into the App Group container and the files -- Copy to Frank -- put into <Documents>/Inbox. It takes no argument, reaches nothing outside those two roots, and moves, parses and deletes nothing -- the inbox is where a thing waits. It gets NO init script: nothing on the page calls it yet, and the spike proves itself with a log line at start-up. Nothing else beyond core:default is granted. NOTE what is deliberately absent: tauri-plugin-deep-link AND tauri-plugin-opener are registered in lib.rs and get NO permission here, so none of their commands are reachable from the page. Both links a phone receives -- frank-pair:// and Google's redirect -- are read in Rust and written into localStorage from there; a page that could call get_current() could read the pass, or another app's redirect, out of a launch URL, and no page needs to. And opener without a permission cannot be asked to open an arbitrary address: google_sign_in opens Google's authorization endpoint or refuses in words.
